title: Why the Best Software Advice Is the Hardest to Follow
why_read: A reasonable, if somewhat generic, reflection on the distinction between clear-cut coding rules and harder-to-apply judgment calls in software engineering.
analysis: This article distinguishes between 'practical advice' in software engineering, like keeping functions small, which is easy to verify and enforce via linters, and 'judgment-based advice,' which requires weighing competing principles without a clear right answer. The piece argues the harder, judgment-based advice tends to be more valuable despite being harder to teach or standardize. It's a fairly common observation in software engineering writing, presented clearly but without deep novel insight or concrete examples of the judgment-based advice it's building toward in the excerpt shown.
